# MLP Neural Fields

Also called: Coordinate-based Neural Fields, Implicit Neural Representations (INRs) via MLPs

## Overview
MLP Neural Fields define a continuous scene function $F_\Theta: \mathbb{R}^d \rightarrow \mathbb{R}^k$ using a Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) to map continuous spatial coordinates (and optionally viewing direction or time) to volumetric signals such as density and color [G]. This family solves the problem of representing complex 3D geometry and appearance in a compact, differentiable format suitable for volume rendering and novel view synthesis [G]. What sets this family apart from sibling methods like [Hash Grid Neural Fields](3855-hash-grid-neural-fields.md) or [Feature Grid as Radiance Field](5508-feature-grid-as-radiance-field.md) is the exclusive reliance on fully connected layers without auxiliary data structures (like hash tables or voxel grids) to store features, relying instead on the network's capacity and [positional encoding](#876-positional-encoding.md) to capture spatial frequencies [G].

## Shared principles
All methods in this family define a scene function $F_\Theta: \mathbb{R}^d \rightarrow \mathbb{R}^k$ using a neural network or a set of parameterized primitives [G]. The input is a continuous coordinate vector (typically 3D spatial position $\mathbf{x}$, potentially augmented with viewing direction $\mathbf{d}$ or time $t$), and the output is a signal vector (e.g., density $\sigma$ and color $\mathbf{c}$) [G]. The network or primitives are trained by minimizing a loss between rendered observations and ground truth images [G]. A critical shared challenge is **spectral bias**, where standard MLPs with smooth activations (like ReLU) struggle to learn high-frequency details, often necessitating specific architectural choices or activation functions [G].

## Subtopics

### [NeRF MLP Architecture](910-nerf-mlp-architecture.md)
The [NeRF MLP Architecture](#910-nerf-mlp-architecture.md) is a multi-layer perceptron (MLP) that implicitly represents a 3D scene as a continuous volumetric function, mapping 3D spatial coordinates and viewing directions to volume density and view-dependent emitted color. It solves the problem of view synthesis by optimizing a neural network to minimize the error between rendered images and observed input images, enabling the generation of photorealistic novel views from sparse input views. What sets it apart from its siblings, such as [Scene Representation Networks (SRN)](1150-scene-representation-networks-srn.md) and [SIREN Neural Field](1250-siren-neural-field.md), is its specific two-branch design that enforces multiview consistency by predicting density as a function of position only, while predicting color as a function of both position and viewing direction, combined with the use of positional encoding to overcome spectral bias.

### [Scene Representation Networks (SRN)](1150-scene-representation-networks-srn.md)
[Scene Representation Networks (SRN)](#1150-scene-representation-networks-srn.md) represent a continuous scene as an opaque surface implicitly defined by a Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) that maps 3D coordinates to feature vectors. Unlike volumetric rendering methods, SRN trains a recurrent neural network to march along rays, using the feature vector at each coordinate to predict the next step size along the ray, and decodes the final feature vector into a single surface color. It is distinguished from its sibling [NeRF MLP Architecture](910-nerf-mlp-architecture.md) by its assumption of an opaque surface rather than a volumetric medium, and from [SIREN Neural Field](1250-siren-neural-field.md) by its use of recurrence for [ray marching](#6739-ray-marching.md) rather than frequency-aware activations for direct coordinate mapping.

### [SIREN Neural Field](1250-siren-neural-field.md)
The SIREN ([Sinusoidal Representation Network](#1250-siren-neural-field.md)) is a neural field that maps continuous coordinates to signal values using sine activations with a specific initialization, allowing it to represent high-frequency detail and have well-behaved derivatives. It solves the problem of spectral bias in standard Multi-Layer Perceptrons (MLPs), which struggle to learn high-frequency signals. Unlike the [MLP Neural Field](1256-mlp-neural-field.md) which typically uses ReLU or similar smooth activations, SIREN uses sine activations throughout (or in the final layer) to enable sharp reconstruction, reaching convergence in ~100 steps where ReLU-MLPs fail even after 2000 steps.

### [MLP Neural Field](1256-mlp-neural-field.md)
A [plain MLP neural field](#1256-mlp-neural-field.md) is a coordinate-based neural network that maps continuous input coordinates to signal values (e.g., density and color) using standard fully connected layers and smooth activation functions like ReLU. It serves as the fundamental baseline for [neural implicit representations](#11368-scene-representation-and-architecture.md), contrasting with specialized architectures like SIREN that use sine activations to overcome spectral bias and represent high-frequency details. Unlike sibling methods that introduce specific architectural modifications for efficiency or surface reconstruction, the plain MLP relies on a standard sequential stack of linear transformations.

### Neural Dependence Fields (NDFs)
**Definition:** Neural Dependence Fields (NDFs) learn the statistical dependencies between spatial locations across ensemble members by mapping pairs of 3D coordinates to Pearson correlation or mutual information values using a bipartite encoder network with multiresolution [hash grids](#936-hash-grids.md) [S1, unofficial].
**Pitfalls:** The method operates on a single time step and tends to smooth fine-scale correlation structures due to hash table capacity constraints [S1, unofficial].
**Performance:** On a 1000-member weather ensemble (250 × 352 × 20), NDFs achieved 87.63 dB PSNR for self-correlation fields with 9 ms inference, 26× faster than GPU-computed Pearson correlation and five orders of magnitude faster than [CPU](#10688-naive-sdf-generation-cpu.md) mutual information estimation, at over 6,000× [compression](#4-compression.md) relative to storing all pairwise correlations [S1, unofficial].

## Background
The concept of implicit neural representations for scenes originated with [Scene Representation Networks (SRN)](1150-scene-representation-networks-srn.md) [S1, unofficial]. The modern paradigm of using MLPs for volumetric rendering was established by [NeRF MLP Architecture](910-nerf-mlp-architecture.md) [S2]. To address the spectral bias inherent in standard MLPs, [SIREN Neural Field](1250-siren-neural-field.md) introduced sinusoidal activations [S2, unofficial]. The family has expanded to include specialized applications such as [Neural Dependence Fields (NDFs)](1256-mlp-neural-field.md) for scientific ensemble data [S1, unofficial].
